extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates or graduate students learning algebraic topology / cohomology
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of singular, simplicial, and cellular cohomology: definitions, key properties (exact sequences, universal coefficient theorem, excision, homotopy invariance, Mayer–Vietoris), and the construction and algebraic properties of the cup product and cohomology ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cochain complex and definition of cohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohomology groups H^n(X; G) are defined as Ker δ / Im δ at C^n(X; G) in the cochain complex ... ← C^{n+1}(X;G) ←^{δ} C^n(X;G) ←^{δ} C^{n-1}(X;G) ← ... with δ^2 = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements of Ker δ are cocycles and elements of Im δ are coboundaries. For a cochain ϕ to be a cocycle means δϕ = ϕ∂ = 0, i.e., ϕ vanishes on boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal Coefficient Theorem for cohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: There are split short exact sequences 0 → Ext(H_{n-1}(X), G) → H^n(X; G) → Hom(H_n(X), G) → 0 describing H^n(X;G) algebraically in terms of homology with Z-coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how cohomology groups with arbitrary coefficients are determined purely algebraically by homology groups; special cases: if homology groups are finitely generated use Corollary 3.3; for field coefficients Ext terms vanish and H^n(X;F) ≈ Hom_F(H_n(X;F),F).

rubrics_metrics.name: H^0 description (path-component functions)
rubrics_metrics.description: For n = 0 the universal coefficient theorem reduces to an isomorphism H^0(X; G) ≈ Hom(H_0(X), G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 0-cochain is a function ϕ: X → G; being a cocycle means ϕ is constant on path-components, so H^0(X;G) is functions from path-components to G (same as Hom(H_0(X),G)); reduced/unreduced difference described via augmentation map whose image are constant functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: H^1 identification
rubrics_metrics.description: H^1(X; G) ≈ Hom(H_1(X), G); if X is path-connected then H_1(X) is the abelianization of π_1(X) and Hom(H_1(X),G) identifies with Hom(π_1(X), G) when G is abelian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequently H^1 can be viewed as homomorphisms from the fundamental group (abelianized) to the coefficient group; the universal coefficient theorem yields this isomorphism since Ext(H_0(X),G)=0 when H_0(X) is free.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced cohomology relation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduced cohomology groups are defined by dualizing the augmented chain complex; H^n(X;G) = 8^n(X;G) for n > 0, with a precise description of H^0 difference via augmentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The augmentation map ε: C_0(X) → Z dualizes to ε^*: Hom(Z,G) → C^0(X;G) giving constant functions; reduced cohomology is functions constant on path-components modulo globally constant functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative cohomology and long exact sequence of a pair
rubrics_metrics.description: For a pair (X,A) dualizing 0 → C_n(A) → C_n(X) → C_n(X,A) → 0 yields 0 ← C^n(A;G) ← C^n(X;G) ← C^n(X,A;G) ← 0 and induces a long exact sequence ... → H^n(X,A;G) →^{j^*} H^n(X;G) →^{i^*} H^n(A;G) →^{δ} H^{n+1}(X,A;G) → ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C^n(X,A;G) can be viewed as functions on singular n-simplices in X that vanish on simplices in A; relative cohomology conceptually simpler because relative cochain group is a subgroup of absolute cochains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturality and duality of connecting homomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a duality between the connecting homomorphism δ: H^n(A;G) → H^{n+1}(X,A;G) in cohomology and ∂: H_{n+1}(X,A) → H_n(A) in homology, expressed via commutative diagrams (hδ = ∂^* h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The description explains how δ is computed by extending cocycles and composing with boundary maps and how this corresponds under the h map to the homology connecting map; shows commutativity by comparing representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Induced homomorphisms and contravariance
rubrics_metrics.description: A map f: X → Y induces cochain maps f^#: C^n(Y;G) → C^n(X;G) and hence homomorphisms f^*: H^n(Y;G) → H^n(X;G); X ↦ H^n(X;G) is a contravariant functor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functorial properties (f g)^* = g^* f^* and id^* = id follow from the corresponding properties on chain maps; applies in relative case as well, with commuting squares in long exact sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality/naturality in relative universal coefficient sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The algebraic universal coefficient theorem applies to relative cohomology since relative chain groups C_n(X,A) are free; maps f:(X,A)→(Y,B) induce commutative diagrams relating the Ext/Hom exact sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This naturality follows from the naturality of algebraic universal coefficient sequences because vertical maps are induced by chain maps f_#: C_n(X,A)→C_n(Y,B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy invariance
rubrics_metrics.description: If f ≃ g : (X,A) → (Y,B) then f^* = g^* : H^n(Y,B) → H^n(X,A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via dualizing the chain homotopy P in homology: from g_# - f_# = ∂P + P∂ we get g^# - f^# = P^* δ + δ P^*, so P^* is a chain homotopy and induces same map on cohomology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excision in cohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: For subspaces Z ⊂ A ⊂ X with closure(Z) contained in interior(A), the inclusion i:(X - Z, A - Z) ↪ (X,A) induces isomorphisms i^*: H^n(X,A;G) → H^n(X - Z, A - Z;G) for all n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from corresponding homology result using naturality of the universal coefficient theorem and the five-lemma; or by dualizing the homology excision proof using chain homotopy equivalences and dual maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Axioms for (reduced) cohomology theories on CW complexes
rubrics_metrics.description: A (reduced) cohomology theory is a sequence of contravariant functors h^n from CW complexes to abelian groups with natural coboundary maps δ: h^n(A) → h^{n+1}(X/A) satisfying: (1) homotopy invariance f^* = g^* for f ≃ g; (2) existence of long exact sequence of a pair; (3) wedge axiom: for a wedge X = ⋁ X_α the product map ∏ i_α^*: h^n(X) → ∏ h^n(X_α) is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes that the third axiom involves direct products (not sums) because Hom(⊕ A_α, G) ≈ ∏ Hom(A_α,G); analogous relative statements and relation between reduced/unreduced cohomology as in homology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicial cohomology equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a simplicial complex and A ⊂ X a subcomplex, then simplicial cochain groups C^n(X,A;G) = Hom(Δ_n(X,A), G) and resulting simplicial cohomology groups H^n_Δ(X,A;G) are isomorphic to singular cohomology H^n(X,A;G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusions of simplicial chain groups into singular chain groups induce isomorphisms on cohomology (Corollary 3.4); canonical isomorphism respects cup products as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cellular cohomology and cellular cochain complex
rubrics_metrics.description: For a CW complex X the cellular cochain complex {H^n(X^n, X^{n-1}; G), d_n} yields H^n(X;G) ≈ Ker d_n / Im d_{n-1}, and this cellular cochain complex is isomorphic to the dual of the cellular chain complex via Hom(-,G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 3.5 proof uses universal coefficient theorem (H^k(X^n,X^{n-1};G)=0 for k ≠ n) and induction; the cellular coboundary maps d_n are compositions δ_n j_n and satisfy d_n d_{n-1} = 0; diagram commutativity uses naturality of h and long exact sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mayer–Vietoris sequence in cohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: If X = int(A) ∪ int(B) then there is a long exact Mayer–Vietoris sequence ... → H^n(X;G) → H^n(A;G) ⊕ H^n(B;G) → H^n(A ∩ B;G) → H^{n+1}(X;G) → ... obtained from the short exact sequence 0 → C^n(A+B;G) →^{ψ} C^n(A;G) ⊕ C^n(B;G) →^{ϕ} C^n(A∩B;G) → 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes ψ as restrictions to A and B and ϕ as the difference of restrictions; relative Mayer–Vietoris for pairs (X,Y)=(A∪B,C∪D) is obtained similarly by considering maps of short exact sequences and applying the five-lemma and duality of free chain complexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of cup product on cochains
rubrics_metrics.description: For cochains ϕ ∈ C^k(X;R) and ψ ∈ C^ℓ(X;R), the cup product ϕ ∪ ψ ∈ C^{k+ℓ}(X;R) is defined by (ϕ ∪ ψ)(σ) = ϕ(σ|[v_0,...,v_k]) · ψ(σ|[v_k,...,v_{k+ℓ}]) where the right-hand side uses multiplication in R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemma 3.6: δ(ϕ ∪ ψ) = δϕ ∪ ψ + (-1)^k ϕ ∪ δψ, so cup product of cocycles is a cocycle and cup product descends to cohomology H^k × H^ℓ → H^{k+ℓ}; if R has 1 then 1 ∈ H^0(X;R) is identity. Examples compute cup products explicitly on surfaces, RP^2, lens spaces, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative and mixed cup products
rubrics_metrics.description: Cup product formula restricts to relative cup products H^k(X;R) × H^ℓ(X,A;R) → H^{k+ℓ}(X,A;R), H^k(X,A;R) × H^ℓ(X;R) → H^{k+ℓ}(X,A;R), and more generally H^k(X,A;R) × H^ℓ(X,B;R) → H^{k+ℓ}(X,A ∪ B;R) for A,B open or subcomplexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction uses subgroups C^n(X,A;R) of cochains vanishing on chains in A and the identification (when A,B open or subcomplexes) that inclusion C^n(X,A∪B) ↪ C^n(X,A+B) induces isomorphisms on cohomology (via excision/five-lemma).

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturality of cup product under maps
rubrics_metrics.description: For a map f: X → Y the induced maps satisfy f^*(α ∪ β) = f^*(α) ∪ f^*(β) (and similarly in the relative case).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof comes from the cochain equality f^#(ϕ) ∪ f^#(ψ) = f^#(ϕ ∪ ψ), verified by evaluating on simplices and using functoriality of composition on singular simplices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graded-commutativity of cup product
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is commutative then α ∪ β = (-1)^{kℓ} β ∪ α for α ∈ H^k(X,A;R) and β ∈ H^ℓ(X,A;R).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses a chain map ρ reversing vertex order with sign ε_n and shows ρ is chain homotopic to identity so on cohomology ρ* disappears; consequences include 2α^2 = 0 for odd-dimensional α and constraints on squares when H^{2k} has no 2-torsion. Detailed constructive proof via prism operator P and sign bookkeeping is given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology as a graded ring (cohomology ring)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define H^*(X;R) = ⊕_{n≥0} H^n(X;R) with multiplication given by cup product, making H^*(X;R) into a (graded) ring (and R-algebra if coefficients considered).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements are finite sums of classes in various degrees; multiplication is bilinear and respects grading (product of degree i and j lies in degree i+j). Examples: H^*(RP^2;Z_2) ≅ Z_2[α]/(α^3), H^*(CP^n;Z) ≅ Z[α]/(α^{n+1}) with |α|=2, etc. Emphasizes graded commutativity (with sign) and that ring-level description often more compact than listing individual groups.
